chunks: And why should you not eat of that over which the name of God has been pronounced, when He has made it distinctly clear what is forbidden, unless you are constrained to do so. Surely many (men) mislead others into following their vain desires through lack of knowledge. Your Lord certainly knows the transgressors.

key_terms.ذُكِرَ اسْمُ اللَّهِ: The name of God was mentioned (during slaughter)

ai.seo_question: What is the rule for eating meat not slaughtered in God's name and what is the exception?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse underscores the theological principle that mere ritual slaughter is insufficient if the meat is not free from the idolatrous associations of the pre-Islamic era, a nuance emphasized by scholars like Al-Tabarsi. The exception for necessity (darura) is interpreted not merely as survival but as a temporary suspension of the prohibition, preserving the sanctity of the divine name while acknowledging human frailty. This connects the physical act of eating with the spiritual state of following one's desires (hawaa) versus adhering to divine knowledge.
